title: China's Top Green Tea Is Fried by Bare Hands — Longjing | China Travel Expert
description:
China's most famous green tea isn't made by machine — it's fried by bare hands in a scorching steel wok.

That tea is Longjing (Dragon Well) from Hangzhou. Masters work the fresh leaves — picked the same morning — through ten named hand movements: shaking, pressing, grinding, straightening and more, switching by feel until the leaf turns flat and sword-like. The wok runs hot enough to blister an untrained palm. In 2022 the craft joined UNESCO's list of Traditional Tea Processing Techniques (national intangible heritage since 2008).

🧭 Expert Tip: For the best cup, buy pre-Qingming (míngqián) leaf — picked before early April — and brew it around 80°C, never with boiling water, so it stays sweet instead of bitter.

中国最有名的绿茶，全靠一双手在铁锅里炒出来。
